answers.answer:
Family a.298.1.1 (TAL effector repeat, superfamily a.298.1, fold a.298 'TAL effector', class a: all-alpha) is defined by the homologous ~34-residue repeat unit, not by chain length. Each TAL repeat is a short helix-loop-helix / two-helix hairpin with the repeat-variable diresidue (RVD, positions 12-13) at the loop; tandem repeats pack into a right-handed solenoid superhelix. SCOPe treats such tandem-repeat solenoids (as it does TPR, ankyrin, LRR, armadillo arrays) as a single domain spanning the whole array, so the domain length simply scales with how many repeats were present in the crystallized or NMR construct.

The three domains differ only in repeat count: d2kq5a_ is the NMR structure of a minimal ~1.5-repeat fragment of Xanthomonas PthA (roughly 50-60 residues); d3v6pa_ is the whole chain of the engineered 11.5-repeat dHax3 array (~400 residues, apo form from Deng et al. 2012); d4cj9a_ is a much longer TALE-like repeat array (the Burkholderia rhizoxinica BurrH/BuD array of ~19 repeats, to my recollection of the Stella et al. 2014 entry; the precise protein should be checked against the SCOPe entry). Because TAL repeats are nearly identical in sequence apart from the RVD (often >80-90% identity repeat-to-repeat and across effectors), SCOPe's automated sequence-based assignment in the 2.0x releases matches any new TALE array to the manually curated a.298.1.1 representative with high confidence, and manual curation of fold a.298 placed the repeat array in one family at the family level (clear sequence homology), not merely at superfamily or fold level. The family/superfamily/fold hierarchy is therefore 'a.298.1.1 = homologous TALE repeats of any copy number', and no length criterion is applied.

Limits: (1) Shared family membership implies common ancestry of the repeat unit and a conserved RVD-based DNA-recognition mode, but it does not transfer the DNA target sequence; each array's specificity depends on its own RVD sequence, so function (target site) cannot be inferred from classification. (2) Template use is asymmetric: d2kq5a_ covers only ~1.5 repeats and cannot by itself define superhelical pitch or inter-repeat packing, while full arrays such as d3v6pa_ change pitch between apo and DNA-bound states (compare 3v6p apo with the DNA-bound 3v6t), so a single representative is not a general template for all TALE conformations. (3) The three entries come from different organisms (Xanthomonas vs Burkholderia TALE-like proteins) and different methods (NMR vs X-ray), so representative selection for the family should prefer a full-length, high-resolution array rather than the short NMR fragment. (4) Exact residue ranges, release of first appearance (fold a.298 was added in the SCOPe 2.06/2.07-era curation), and the identity of 4cj9's protein should be confirmed against the current SCOPe release, since I am answering from pretrained knowledge without network access.
